newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Court tells German builders honour wage vow.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Court tells German builders honour wage vow.

text.p: A court on Wednesday ruled that the German building industry should honour wage contracts designed to bring east German wages up to western levels, after an unprecedented cancellation of the contracts.

An industrial tribunal in Wiesbaden ruled null and void the move by builders last August to cancel the contracts, which the industry had blamed on an exceptionally tight economic squeeze on construction firms in the once-booming eastern states.

The building industry said it would consider an appeal against the ruling while the IG Bau trade union, which had filed a complaint against the cancellation of contracts, demanded that employers immediately pay out the wage increases in arrears.

The contracts in question would have put in place a 1.85 percent wage rise from September 1 1996 as well as an accompanying agreement to gradually push average east German wages up to 95 percent of west German levels from 92 percent.
In a statement, the building industry association Hauptverband der Deutschen Bauindustrie said it would decide on February 26 whether to appeal the ruling.
The association defended its decision to cancel the wage contracts and appealed to unions not to put too much pressure on east German building firms.

"Clearly we did not succeed in convincing the Wiesbaden tribunal of the unusually pressured situation in which building firms and associations found themselves in late summer 1996 and in which they still are," said Wilhelm Kuechler, the association's vice-president.
Kuechler noted that 1996 had seen a 1.7 percent real drop in east German building spending -- the first decline since unification.

Eastern firms had been further pressured by foreign competitors outbidding their German rivals by paying lower wages, insolvencies rose 50 percent to 1,850 firms, and more than 30,000 jobs had to be shed.

"We had to act to prevent anything worse from happening," Kuechler said. "It will not help IG Bau either if the existence of east German (building) asssociations is threatened by excessive wage demands."
